import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 20

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/20](https://www.erdosproblems.com/20)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics))
* [ErRa60] Erdős, Paul and Rado, Richard. Intersection theorems for systems of sets.
  J. London Math. Soc. 35 (1960), 85--90.

-/
namespace Erdos20

/--
Let $f(n,k)$ be minimal such that every $F$ family of $n$-uniform sets with $|F| \ge f(n,k)$
contains a $k$-sunflower.
-/
noncomputable def f (n k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m | ∀ {α : Type}, ∀ (F : Set (Set α)),
    ((∀ f ∈ F, f.ncard = n) ∧ m ≤ F.ncard) → ∃ S ⊆ F, S.ncard = k ∧ IsSunflower S}

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem f_0_1 : f 0 1 = 1 := by
  refine IsLeast.csInf_eq ⟨fun F hF ↦ ?_, fun n hn ↦ n.pos_of_ne_zero fun hn₀ ↦ ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := F.nonempty_of_ncard_ne_zero (by omega)
    exact ⟨{A}, by simpa using ⟨hA, isSunflower_singleton _⟩⟩
  · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := (hn (α := ℕ) {} (by simpa))
    simp_all [bot_unique hS.1]

/--
Is it true that $f(n,k) < c_k^n$ for some constant $c_k>0$ and for all $n > 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_20 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (c : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ n k, n > 0 → f n k < (c k) ^ n := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the various known bounds as variants.

/--
Erdős and Rado [ErRa60] proved the factorial upper bound for the $k$-sunflower
threshold: any family of $n$-uniform sets with more than $(k-1)^n \, n!$ members
contains a $k$-sunflower, hence $f(n,k) \le (k-1)^n \, n! + 1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/HowieHwong/lean-erdos-proofs/blob/b8b641ba2d00dc4d1fe205a078a4159372672459/Erdos/P20.lean#L202"]
theorem erdos_20.variants.erdos_rado_bound :
    ∀ n k, n > 0 → 2 ≤ k → f n k ≤ (k - 1) ^ n * n.factorial + 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos20

findings.description: The uniformity condition `∀ A ∈ F, A.ncard = n` admits infinite members when `n = 0`, since `Set.ncard` returns 0 on infinite sets. Consequently, `f 0 3 = 0`, rather than the intended threshold 2. For every m, take the finite family of m distinct infinite tails `{Set.Ici i | i < m}` in ℕ. Each member has ncard 0, but no three distinct tails form a sunflower. Thus no m satisfies the defining property, and `sInf ∅ = 0`. In contrast, a genuine 0-uniform family of distinct sets is contained in `{∅}`: threshold 1 fails, while threshold 2 works vacuously. Both values were proved in `/workspace/review/boundary.lean` without `sorry`. This defect concerns the definition at zero; both research theorems explicitly require `n > 0`.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/20 defines f(n,k) as the minimum forcing size for families of n-uniform sets, using |F| ≥ f(n,k). The cited Wikipedia article, section “Sunflower lemma and conjecture,” explicitly defines the parameters for nonnegative integers, requires actual bounded cardinality of each member, and describes the convention in which sets appear at most once. At uniformity zero, the only such member is the empty set.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the member condition by `∀ A ∈ F, A.Finite ∧ A.ncard = n`, or equivalently use `∀ A ∈ F, A.encard = (n : ℕ∞)`. Adding only `F.Finite` would not fix the problem: the counterexample families are already finite. Add a regression test asserting that the corrected definition has `f 0 3 = 2`. The suggested finite-member repair was also proved equal to the current definition for every `n > 0`.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses one function `c : ℕ → ℕ`, omits an explicit positivity hypothesis, and includes k = 0, 1, 2. The usual formulation uses a positive real constant for each fixed k ≥ 3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any positive real constant can be rounded upward to a natural number, and the choices for each k form a function. Conversely, the Lean inequality at n = 1 forces every c(k) to be positive, and natural constants can be cast to ℝ. The extra petal cases are automatic: f(n,0) = 0, f(n,1) = 1, and f(n,2) = 2, with constants 1, 2, and 3 respectively. The complete equivalence with the positive-real, k ≥ 3 formulation was kernel-checked as `Review.conjecture_restricted_petals_iff`.

reformulations.difference: Lean states `f n k ≤ (k - 1)^n * n.factorial + 1`, whereas Wikipedia presents the classical lemma in the family form “more than (k−1)^n n! members.”
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing B = (k−1)^n n!, a finite family has more than B members exactly when it has at least B+1 members. Thus the minimum forcing size under this file’s ≥ convention is at most B+1. Conversely, a forcing threshold at most B+1 gives the stated family-form lemma. The classical sunflower lemma ensures that the threshold set is nonempty in the declared range. A sunflower with at least k members can be reduced to exactly k. The endpoint adjustment is necessary: the separately verified identity f(1,k) = k makes this bound exact at n = 1.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/20 — statement, remarks, and current OPEN status; read through https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/20 using its HTML response after direct access returned a Cloudflare challenge.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics) — definitions, threshold conventions, sunflower lemma, conjecture, and variants.
Erdős and Rado, “Intersection theorems for systems of sets,” J. London Math. Soc. 35 (1960), 85–90: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1960-04.pdf
Alweiss, Lovett, Wu, and Zhang, “Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma,” introduction and subsequent-work discussion; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1908.08483
Local definition sources: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SetFamily/Sunflower.lean; Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean; Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. `f_0_1` has the intended value. For positive uniformity, member finiteness follows from nonzero ncard; infinite ambient families do not change the forcing threshold because finite subfamilies suffice. The source still records the main conjecture as open. The exact cited formal proof of the factorial bound compiled, and both its family-form theorem and threshold theorem depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary proofs, equivalence proofs, and small finite sunflower tests are saved under /workspace/review/.

submission.summary: Required each member of a uniform family to be finite, preventing infinite sets from being treated as zero-element sets. Added the proved regression test `Erdos20.f_0_3 : f 0 3 = 2`. Verified that the definition is unchanged for positive n and that both boundary tests use only standard axioms. The required compile command reports only the two existing `sorry` warnings.

  · intro α F hF

      exact Set.mem_singleton_iff.mpr ((Set.ncard_eq_zero (hF.1 A hA).1).mp (hF.1 A hA).2)
    have hc := Set.ncard_le_ncard hsub (Set.finite_singleton _)
    simp only [Set.ncard_singleton] at hc
    omega
  · intro m hm
    by_contra h
    have hm' : m ≤ 1 := by omega
    obtain ⟨S, hS, hSc, -⟩ := hm (α := ℕ) {∅} (by simpa using hm')
    have hc := Set.ncard_le_ncard hS (Set.finite_singleton _)
    simp only [Set.ncard_singleton] at hc
    omega
